## Data Loading and Tidying ONLY DO ONCE

#### Merge all of the C and N tin plate runs into one dataframe

```{r}
    ## Do only once to tidy raw data for subsequent analyses

    #load data 
    CN2 <-read.csv("C:/Users/iemus/Documents/UW_MS_LAVOSoils/MSWhitman/LAVO_FireHistory/Data/RAW/Whitman Muscettola CN 032824.csv")
    CN1 <-read.csv("C:/Users/iemus/Documents/UW_MS_LAVOSoils/MSWhitman/LAVO_FireHistory/Data/RAW/Whitman Muscettola CN 051424.csv")
    CN3 <- read.csv("C:/Users/iemus/Documents/UW_MS_LAVOSoils/MSWhitman/LAVO_FireHistory/Data/RAW/CN results for LAV022 Elm.csv")
    CN4 <- read.csv("C:/Users/iemus/Documents/UW_MS_LAVOSoils/MSWhitman/LAVO_FireHistory/Data/RAW/CN results Emily Kaufman and Isabella Muscetola 032026.csv")

    #add column with analysis date and run number
    CN2$Date <- 20240328
    CN1$Date <- 20240514
    CN3$Date <- 20250809
    CN4$Date <-202603
    CN2$Run <- 1
    CN1$Run <- 1
    CN3$Run <- 2
    CN4$Run <- 3

    #add Notes column to CN3
    CN3$Notes <- ""
    CN4 <- rename(CN4, Notes = Issue)
    
    #fix data type of CN4 from character to double
    CN4$X.N <- as.numeric(CN4$X.N)
    CN4$X.C <- as.numeric(CN4$X.C)

    #merge datasets from EA analysis runs 1, 2, and 3 
    temp <- rbind(CN1, CN2)
    temp2 <- bind_rows(temp, CN3)
    CN <- bind_rows(temp2, CN4)
    rm(temp, temp2)

    #rename column X.N and X.C to percN and percC
    CN <- CN %>%
      rename(percN = X.N) %>%
      rename(percC = X.C)

    #add columns removing data for samples with percent below or above detection limit 
    CN <- CN %>%
    mutate(cleanN = ifelse(Notes=="N below detection limit", NA, ifelse(Notes=="CN below detection limit",NA,percN))) %>% 
      mutate(cleanC = ifelse(Notes=="C above detection limit",
    NA, ifelse(Notes=="CN below detection limit", NA, percC)))

    #separate out samples that were rerun 
    #rerunsamples <- CN |> group_by(Sample.Name) |> filter(n()>1) |> ungroup()
    
    #write.csv(rerunsamples, "C:/Users/iemus/Documents/UW_MS_LAVOSoils/MSWhitman/LAVO_FireHistory/Data/R/CarbonNitrogen/CN_rerunsamples.csv")
    

    #what were the issues with the samples that needed to be rerun?
    #temp <- CN %>% 
    #  group_by(Notes) %>% 
    #  summarise(count=n()) 
    #rm(temp)

    #save CN merged dataframe
    write.csv(CN,"C:/Users/iemus/Documents/UW_MS_LAVOSoils/MSWhitman/LAVO_FireHistory/Data/R/CarbonNitrogen/CN_allruns_merged.csv")
    

# the merged CN dataframe includes multiple runs of the same samples. This is either a) because the sample was accidentally ran twice, b) because the sample was run and at least one of the C or N values was outside of detection limits, c) the sample was run and did not return any data for C or N. This function finds the duplicates based on the Sample.Name. Then among the duplicates it will keep only one row - 1) ideally a row where both cleanC & clean N are numbers (i.e. not NA) or 2) keep a row where at least one of the two is a number
    
#NOTE: 2 errors in sample name was identified in the QA/QC - corrections were made to the csv and file was named "CN_allruns_merged_corrected.csv" this merged csv should be used for subsequent analyses.
    
    #CN <- read.csv("C:/Users/iemus/Documents/UW_MS_LAVOSoils/MSWhitman/LAVO_FireHistory/Data/R/CarbonNitrogen/CN_allruns_merged_corrected.csv")

#above QA/QC correction was added by using 2026 run C/N data. 
    CN <- read.csv("C:/Users/iemus/Documents/UW_MS_LAVOSoils/MSWhitman/LAVO_FireHistory/Data/R/CarbonNitrogen/CN_allruns_merged.csv")

    CN_tidy <- CN %>%
  group_by(Sample.Name) %>%
  #create a "score" based on our preferences outlined above for cleanC & cleanN values
  mutate(score = case_when(
    !is.na(cleanC) & ! is.na(cleanN) ~2, #both present
    !is.na(cleanC) | !is.na(cleanN) ~1, #one present
    TRUE ~ 0 #both NA
  )) %>%
  #keep the rows with the highest score
  filter(score == max(score)) %>%
  # in case of ties, pick the first occurrence
  slice(1) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(!score) %>%
  #rename "Date" column to "CN Analysis Date" & "Weight" to "CN_Weight"
  rename(CN_Analysis_Date = Date, CN_Weight = Weight) %>%
  #select relevant columns to the metadata and subsequent analyses
  select(Sample.Name, CN_Analysis_Date, CN_Weight:cleanC)
    
    #replace " " in Sample.Name with "_" so that it matches the Sample Name in the metadata
    CN_tidy$Sample.Name <- gsub(" ", "_", CN_tidy$Sample.Name)
    
    write.csv(CN_tidy, "C:/Users/iemus/Documents/UW_MS_LAVOSoils/MSWhitman/LAVO_FireHistory/Data/R/CarbonNitrogen/CN_merged_final.csv")
    
rm(CN1, CN2, CN3, CN4, temp, CN, rerunsamples)
```


## Summarize Carbon Stocks
Since only 1 bulk density core was taken at select plots, the 3 replicates (A, B, and C) have the same bulk density but distict C concentrations. One way of dealing with this nested plot design is by taking the average of the 3 replicates for 1 Carbon Stock per plot. In order to do that we must summarize the dataframe by Plot_Horizon

```{r}
temp <- df %>%
  group_by(Plot_Horizon) %>%
  summarise(mean_Cstock_gcm2 = mean(Cstock_gcm2), sd_Cstock_gcm2 = sd(Cstock_gcm2)) %>%
  filter(str_ends(Plot_Horizon, "M")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(mean_Cstock_gcm2))

temp2 <- select(df, c(Plot_Horizon, Unit:Horizon, Soil_mu:Slope, Wt_Avg_QuadBS, Veg_Type:Soil_Series, Sand_perc:Texture_Name, Volume.of.rocks..mL.:bdof2mmfraction_gcm3))

Cstock_summary <- left_join(temp2, temp, by="Plot_Horizon") %>%
  filter(., !is.na(mean_Cstock_gcm2))

#now let's make a dataframe with the Cstock summarized by Unit and Trt
temp <- df %>%
  filter(!is.na(Cstock_gcm2)) %>%
  group_by(Unit, Trt) %>%
  summarise(mean_Cstock_gcm2=mean(Cstock_gcm2), sd_Cstock_gcm2 = sd(Cstock_gcm2), n=n())

#let's save the dataframe for Manuscript figure
Cstock_summary <- temp %>%
  mutate('Carbon Stock g/cm2' = paste0(round(mean_Cstock_gcm2, digits=1), " (±", round(sd_Cstock_gcm2, digits=1), ")")) %>%
  select(1:2, 5:6)

write.csv(Cstock_summary, "C:/Users/iemus/Documents/UW_MS_LAVOSoils/MSWhitman/LAVO_FireHistory/Figures/CN/Cstock_byunitandtreatment.csv", row.names = FALSE)

#now let's make a dataframe with the Cstock summarized by Unit only
temp <- df %>%
  filter(!is.na(Cstock_gcm2)) %>%
  group_by(Unit) %>%
  summarise(mean_Cstock_gcm2=mean(Cstock_gcm2), sd_Cstock_gcm2=sd(Cstock_gcm2), n=n())

Cstock_summary <- temp %>%
  mutate('Carbon Stock g/cm2'=paste0(round(mean_Cstock_gcm2, digits=1), " (±", round(sd_Cstock_gcm2, digits=1), ")")) %>%
  select(1, 4:5)

write.csv(Cstock_summary, "C:/Users/iemus/Documents/UW_MS_LAVOSoils/MSWhitman/LAVO_FireHistory/Figures/CN/Cstock_byunit.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

## Statistics

linear mixed model with random effects of plot and core

### % C Model selection

```{r}
#Forwards model selection 
#Horizon 
mod.hor <- lmer(percC ~ Horizon + (1|Plot_Name/Rep), data=df.noUB) 
summary(mod.hor) 
anova(mod.hor)
#horizon is significant; p=2.2e-16

#Unit 
mod.unit <- lmer(percC~Unit + (1|Plot_Name/Rep), data=df.noUB)
anova(mod.unit) 
# \*\*\* p=1.6e-8

#Soil subgroup 
mod.soil <- lmer(percC~Soil_Subgroup + (1|Plot_Name/Rep), data=df.noUB) 
anova(mod.soil) 
# \*\*\* p=0.0002097

#Sample severity
```

```{r}
############ %C contrasts

###post hoc test on final model 
#fire history contrasts 
con.trt <- emmeans(finalmod.C, pairwise~Trt) 
t <- as.data.frame(con.trt$contrasts) %>% 
  mutate(., Unit=NA, Horizon=NA, SampleSev=NA) #save as a dataframe to merge with other contrasts

#burn severity contrasts 
con.samplesevbyhorizon <-emmeans(finalmod.C, pairwise~SampleSev|Horizon) 
con.samplesevbyhorizon #Mineral horizons no sig difference by burn severity #Organic horizons: 1&2 < 3&4 
ss.by.h <- as.data.frame(con.samplesevbyhorizon$contrasts) %>% 
  mutate(., SampleSev=NA, Unit=NA)

###what if allowed for 3-way interaction: 
#mod.u.h.ss.3.t <- lmer(percC~Unit*Horizon*SampleSev+Trt+(1|Plot_Name/Rep), data=df.noUB)
#test <- emmeans(mod.u.h.ss.3.t, pairwise~SampleSev|Unit+Horizon)
#test #mineral horizons no sig diff by burn severity; #O: BL no sig diff; H: 1 >2 & 1>4, but 1=3; WV: 2>3&4

con.horbyunitsamplesev <- emmeans(mod.u.h.2.ss.2.t, pairwise~Horizon|Unit+SampleSev) 
con.horbyunitsamplesev # O %C \> M %C except in burn sev class 4 in Butte Lake where O & M %C are equal
h.by.ss <- as.data.frame(con.horbyunitsamplesev$contrasts) %>%
  mutate(., Horizon=NA)

con.unitbyhorizon <-emmeans(mod.u.h.2.ss.2.t, pairwise~Unit|Horizon)
con.unitbyhorizon # Mineral: BL & H \<\< WV; Organic: BL \< H \< WV
u.by.h <- as.data.frame(con.unitbyhorizon$contrasts) %>% 
  mutate(., Unit=NA, SampleSev=NA)

#bind together relevant contrasts 
con.df <- rbind(ss.by.h, h.by.ss)
con.df <- rbind(con.df, u.by.h) 
con.df <- rbind(con.df, t)

write.csv(con.df, "C:/Users/iemus/Documents/UW_MS_LAVOSoils/MSWhitman/LAVO_FireHistory/Data/R/CarbonNitrogen/Cmodel_contrasts.csv")
rm(con.horbyunitsamplesev, con.all.df, con.trt.df, con.unit.df, con.samplesevbyunithor, con.trt, con.unitbyhorizon, t, ss.by.u.h, h.by.ss, u.by.h)

C.con.df <- con.df 
rm(con.df)
```
